correctness.rationale: The barycentric Gram matrix gives an explicit reproducing kernel. Minimization over bounded nonnegative inputs is the negative kernel mass. Convexity of the positive-part affine function proves that this mass is maximized at a vertex, where a Beta(1,d) integral evaluates exactly to the claimed constant. Kernel normalization gives the exact L-infinity norm. The packaged exact-rational replay returns VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: Local L2 projection onto linear finite-element spaces is a standard numerical operation, and positivity is a basic structural constraint. The theorem gives a complete sharp diagnosis on the elementary building block: exact negative excursion, exact L-infinity norm, explicit extremizer, strict-positive failure, shape independence, and linear dimension growth. The defect exceeding the entire input amplitude in three dimensions is a substantive design and testing fact.
